en: The Apadāna of the Elder Pubbaṅgamiya from the Paṇṇadāyakavagga of the Therāpadāna, Number Ten.
“Eighty-four thousand of us went forth as renunciants, possessing nothing;
I was the leader among them.”
For the attainment of the supreme goal,
these beings— though still possessing passion—
are serene and undisturbed in mind.
With serene hearts, they respectfully served them with their own hands—
those whose taints were destroyed and whose faults were vomited out.
Having fulfilled their tasks and being free from taints,
the self-become ones, unconquered, pervaded [all beings] with a mind of loving-kindness.
Having attended upon those perfectly enlightened ones with mindfulness,
death has now arrived.
And you have gone to the state of the gods.
Because I maintained this virtue for ninety-four eons, [I have attained this result].
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of mindfulness.
There are four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā).
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Pubbaṅgamiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Pubbaṅgamiya is the tenth.
The Paṇṇadāyaka Chapter is the thirty-ninth. Its summary (uddāna) is as follows:
Paṇṇa, Phala, Paccuggama,
Ekapupphi, and Maghavā;
and the Upaṭṭhākāpāda.
The going forth, the attendant of the Buddha,
and the forty-eight verses praised as the precursors.
